detailed_description: The ASCII Table is a browser reference for character codes and byte-style representations. Browse standard ASCII values from 0 to 127, optionally show the 128 to 255 extended range, and search by decimal value, hex value, displayed character, or description. Each row shows decimal, hexadecimal, octal, binary, character, and a short label; clicking a row opens a selected-character panel with the same values. Printable characters can be copied directly from the character button. It is a quick reference for control characters, printable symbols, logs, tests, and encoding lessons.
usage_steps: Browse the table to find a character or code value.
Search by decimal number, hex value, character, or description.
Click a row to open the selected-character details panel.
Use Show Extended ASCII if you also want to display values 128-255.
Click a printable character button to copy that character to the clipboard.
usage_examples: Find the newline character as decimal 10 and hex 0A.
Look up uppercase A as decimal 65, hex 41, octal 101, and binary 01000001.
Check control character labels when reading protocol or log documentation.
Copy a printable punctuation mark from the table while preparing test data.

faqs.question: What values are shown by default?
faqs.answer: The default table shows standard ASCII values from 0 to 127.

faqs.question: Can I show values 128 to 255?
faqs.answer: Yes. Enable Show Extended ASCII to add the 128-255 range displayed by the browser.

faqs.question: Which code formats are included?
faqs.answer: Each row includes decimal, hexadecimal, octal, binary, the character display, and a short description.

faqs.question: Can I copy characters?
faqs.answer: Yes. Printable characters can be copied by clicking the character button in the table.

faqs.question: Is extended ASCII the same in every encoding?
faqs.answer: No. Values above 127 vary by code page, so treat the extended range as a convenient browser display, not a universal standard.
